reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's a Wednesday in late August. Nothing special about it on paper. The summer is winding down but hasn't given up yet. You wake up, and there's no wreckage to sort through. No phone you're afraid to check. No apology to draft in your head before your feet hit the floor. That, right there, is the thing they don't tell you about when you're 22 and picturing sobriety as a life sentence in a church basement.

When I got sober, I thought the payoff would be dramatic — some big cinematic transformation. It wasn't. The payoff was a Wednesday. It was making coffee without shaking. Answering a text the same day I got it. Going to work and actually being there. The small ordinary things stacked up, and one day I looked around and realized I had built a life I didn't need to escape from.

Durant, paraphrasing Aristotle, was talking about virtue, but he could've been talking about recovery. You don't become someone you can live with in one grand gesture. You become that person Wednesday by Wednesday. Show up. Do the small thing. Make the bed, keep the appointment, tell the truth about something minor. The life you want isn't waiting on the other side of some breakthrough. It's being built right now, in whatever ordinary hour you're in.
reflection.meditation: What small, ordinary thing can I show up for today that the drinking version of me would have skipped?

affirmations: I am building a life out of ordinary days, not waiting on a dramatic one.
Today I get to be present for whatever actually happens.
I am someone who follows through on the small things, and that is not small.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a quiet morning and a clear head to meet it with. Grateful for the people who stayed while I figured this out, and for the ones I've met on the other side of it. Grateful that a Wednesday in August can just be a Wednesday now — not a crisis, not a hangover, not a countdown to the next drink. That's the whole gift.
gratitude.closing: One more day. One more chance to show up as myself.
